questions.topic: Physics: Mechanics and Properties of Matter
questions.q: The dimensional formula of Planck's constant h is
questions.explanation: h = E/ν, so [h] = ML²T⁻² / T⁻¹ = ML²T⁻¹.

questions.topic: Physics: Mechanics and Properties of Matter
questions.q: A ball is dropped from the top of an 80 m tall tower (g = 10 m/s²). Find its speed just before hitting the ground.
questions.explanation: Free fall from rest gives v = √(2gh) = 40 m/s.

questions.topic: Physics: Mechanics and Properties of Matter
questions.q: A car travels on a level circular road of radius 20 m with coefficient of friction 0.5 (g = 10 m/s²). The maximum speed at which it can turn without skidding is

questions.topic: Physics: Mechanics and Properties of Matter
questions.q: A constant force of 5 N acts on a body and displaces it by 4 m in a direction making 60° with the force. Find the work done.
questions.explanation: Work = F s cos 60° = 20 × 0.5 = 10 J.

questions.topic: Physics: Mechanics and Properties of Matter
questions.q: A body of mass m moving with speed u collides elastically head-on with a stationary body of mass 2m. The speed of the heavier body after the collision is
questions.explanation: For an elastic collision v₂ = 2m₁u/(m₁ + m₂) = 2mu/3m = 2u/3 (the lighter body rebounds at u/3).

questions.topic: Physics: Mechanics and Properties of Matter
questions.q: A planet has the same mass as the Earth but one-fourth of its radius. Taking the escape velocity of Earth as 11.2 km/s, the escape velocity from this planet is
questions.explanation: ve = √(2GM/R) ∝ 1/√R; reducing R to a quarter doubles ve to 22.4 km/s.

questions.topic: Physics: Mechanics and Properties of Matter
questions.q: A solid sphere rolls without slipping on a horizontal surface. The fraction of its total kinetic energy that is rotational is
questions.explanation: KE_rot = ½(2/5 MR²)(v/R)² = (1/5)Mv²; total = (7/10)Mv²; ratio = 2/7.

questions.topic: Physics: Mechanics and Properties of Matter
questions.q: The surface tension of a soap solution is 0.03 N/m. Find the excess pressure inside a soap bubble of radius 2 cm.
keyPoints: A soap bubble has two surfaces: ΔP = 4T/r
questions.explanation: A soap bubble has two liquid surfaces, so ΔP = 4T/r = 6 Pa.

questions.q: The SI unit of specific heat capacity is
questions.explanation: Specific heat c = Q/(mΔT), measured in joule per kilogram per kelvin.

questions.q: How much heat is required to melt 50 g of ice at 0 °C into water at 0 °C? (Latent heat of fusion of ice = 80 cal/g)
questions.explanation: Heat for phase change at constant temperature is Q = mL = 4000 cal.

questions.q: A monatomic ideal gas is heated at constant pressure. The fraction of the heat supplied that is converted into work is
A travelling wave is described by y = 5 sin(200πt − 4πx) in SI units. The speed of the wave is

An unknown tuning fork produces 4 beats per second with a 256 Hz fork. When the unknown fork is loaded with a little wax, the beat frequency decreases to 2 beats per second. Find the original frequency of the unknown fork.
keyPoints: Original frequency is 252 Hz or 260 Hz
Wax lowers the frequency; beats decrease only if it started above 256 Hz, so 260 Hz
questions.explanation: If it were 252 Hz, waxing would lower it and increase the beats. The beats fell, so the fork was at 260 Hz (and dropped to 258 Hz).

questions.q: A stationary source emits sound of frequency 500 Hz. An observer moves towards it at 34 m/s (speed of sound = 340 m/s). The frequency heard is
When the temperature of a semiconductor is increased, its resistivity
questions.explanation: More charge carriers are generated at higher temperature, so the resistivity of a semiconductor falls.

questions.q: A wire of resistance 10 Ω is uniformly stretched to three times its original length. Find its new resistance.
questions.explanation: R = ρl/A and A falls to one-third, so R becomes 3 × 3 = 9 times, i.e. 90 Ω.

questions.q: In a balanced Wheatstone bridge, P = 10 Ω, Q = 20 Ω and R = 30 Ω. The resistance S in the fourth arm (opposite to R, with P/Q = R/S) is
questions.explanation: P/Q = R/S gives S = QR/P = 20 × 30/10 = 60 Ω.

questions.q: A circular coil of 100 turns and radius 10 cm carries a current of 1 A. Find the magnetic field at its centre in terms of π (μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T m/A).
questions.explanation: Substituting in B = μ₀NI/2R gives 2π × 10⁻⁴ T.

questions.q: An LC circuit has L = 1 mH and C = 10 μF. Find its natural angular frequency of oscillation.
questions.explanation: LC = 10⁻⁸ s², so ω = 1/10⁻⁴ = 10⁴ rad/s.

questions.q: A conducting rod of length 0.5 m moves at 4 m/s perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T, with the rod perpendicular to both. The motional emf induced is

questions.topic: Physics: Optics, Modern Physics and Electronics
questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment, the slit separation is halved and the distance of the screen is doubled. The fringe width becomes
questions.explanation: β = λD/d; D doubled and d halved gives 2 × 2 = 4 times.

questions.topic: Physics: Optics, Modern Physics and Electronics
questions.q: An equilateral prism (A = 60°) has refractive index √3. Find the angle of minimum deviation.

questions.topic: Physics: Optics, Modern Physics and Electronics
questions.q: Light travels from water (refractive index 4/3) to air. The critical angle C satisfies

questions.topic: Physics: Optics, Modern Physics and Electronics
questions.q: Light of frequency f incident on a metal of work function 2 eV gives a stopping potential of 2 V. If the frequency is doubled, the stopping potential becomes
questions.explanation: hf = 2 + 2 = 4 eV. Doubling the frequency gives 8 eV, so eVs = 8 − 2 = 6 eV.

questions.topic: Physics: Optics, Modern Physics and Electronics
questions.q: Find the de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through a potential difference of 100 V. (Use λ = 12.27/√V Å)
questions.explanation: Substituting V = 100 V gives λ ≈ 1.23 Å.

questions.topic: Physics: Optics, Modern Physics and Electronics
questions.q: The binding energy per nucleon is greatest for nuclei having mass number around
questions.explanation: The binding energy per nucleon curve peaks near A ≈ 56 (iron), making these nuclei the most stable.

questions.q: The quantum number that determines the shape of an orbital is
questions.explanation: The azimuthal (angular momentum) quantum number ℓ gives the subshell and orbital shape (s, p, d, f).

questions.q: Find the molality of a solution containing 18 g of glucose (molar mass 180 g/mol) dissolved in 500 g of water.
questions.explanation: Molality = moles of solute per kg of solvent = 0.1/0.5 = 0.2.

questions.q: Calculate the elevation in boiling point when 6 g of urea (molar mass 60 g/mol) is dissolved in 200 g of water. (Kb for water = 0.52 K kg/mol)
What volume does 3.2 g of oxygen gas (O₂, molar mass 32 g/mol) occupy at STP? (Molar volume at STP = 22.4 L/mol)
questions.explanation: 0.1 mol of any ideal gas occupies 2.24 L at STP.

questions.q: A reaction with ΔH negative and ΔS positive is
questions.explanation: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS is negative at every temperature when ΔH < 0 and ΔS > 0.

questions.q: Given ΔH for C(s) + O₂(g) → CO₂(g) = −393.5 kJ/mol and for CO(g) + ½O₂(g) → CO₂(g) = −283.0 kJ/mol, find ΔH for C(s) + ½O₂(g) → CO(g).
keyPoints: Subtract the second equation from the first (Hess's law)

questions.q: For the Daniell cell, E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V and E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V. The standard cell potential is
questions.explanation: E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = 0.34 − (−0.76) = 1.10 V.

questions.q: Calculate ΔG° (in kJ/mol) for a cell reaction with n = 2 and E°cell = 1.10 V. (F = 96500 C/mol)
Which 0.1 m aqueous solution (assuming complete dissociation) shows the maximum depression in freezing point?
questions.explanation: CaCl₂ gives three particles (i = 3), more than NaCl (2) and the non-electrolytes (1).

questions.q: Which of the following isoelectronic species has the largest radius?
questions.explanation: All have 10 electrons; the lowest nuclear charge (O²⁻, Z = 8) holds the electrons least tightly, giving the largest size.

questions.q: The atomic radii of Zr and Hf are nearly equal because of
questions.explanation: The poor shielding of 4f electrons causes lanthanoid contraction, offsetting the size increase down the group.

questions.q: Among HF, HCl, HBr and HI, the compound with the highest boiling point is
questions.explanation: Strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding in HF raises its boiling point above the others.

questions.q: Permanent hardness of water can be removed by
questions.explanation: Calgon forms soluble complexes with Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions; boiling and Clark's method remove only temporary hardness.

questions.q: Graphite conducts electricity because
options: it has free delocalised π electrons within layers
its layers are held by covalent bonds
questions.explanation: Each carbon in graphite is sp² hybridised, leaving one electron in a p orbital that is delocalised over the layer.

questions.q: The number of lone pairs on the central atom of XeF₂ is
questions.explanation: Xe has 8 valence electrons; 2 are used in bonds, leaving 3 lone pairs (trigonal bipyramidal geometry, linear shape).

questions.q: When excess AgNO₃ is added to a solution of [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]Cl₂, how many moles of AgCl precipitate per mole of the complex?
keyPoints: Only the Cl⁻ outside the coordination sphere ionises
questions.explanation: The complex ionises to [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]²⁺ and 2Cl⁻; coordinated Cl does not precipitate.

questions.q: In the electrolytic extraction of aluminium (Hall–Héroult process), cryolite is added to alumina in order to
options: lower the melting point and increase conductivity
questions.explanation: Na₃AlF₆ lowers the melting point of the mixture and makes it a better conductor.

questions.q: The general formula of alkynes is
questions.explanation: Each triple bond removes four hydrogens from the alkane formula, giving CnH2n−2.

questions.q: Which of the following shows geometrical (cis–trans) isomerism?
questions.explanation: Only but-2-ene has two different groups on each carbon of the double bond.

questions.q: Which of the following compounds is optically active?
questions.explanation: In CH₃CHClCH₂CH₃ the second carbon has four different groups (a chiral centre).

questions.q: Which alkyl bromide undergoes hydrolysis fastest by the SN1 mechanism?
questions.explanation: The tertiary alkyl halide gives the most stable carbocation intermediate.

questions.q: Ethanol heated with concentrated H₂SO₄ at 443 K gives mainly
questions.explanation: At 443 K intramolecular dehydration gives ethene; at 413 K with excess alcohol ether forms.

questions.q: Which of the following undergoes aldol condensation in dilute alkali?
questions.explanation: Aldol condensation needs an α-hydrogen; ethanal has one, while the others have none.

questions.q: How many π electrons are present in the delocalised cloud of benzene?
keyPoints: Six sp² carbons each contribute one p electron
questions.explanation: Each of the six carbons contributes one electron to the π cloud, making 6 π electrons.

questions.q: Benzene diazonium chloride reacts with phenol in alkaline medium to give
questions.explanation: Coupling at the para position of the phenoxide gives an orange azo dye.

questions.q: The number of chiral carbon atoms in the open-chain structure of D-glucose is
questions.explanation: Glucose (an aldohexose) has asymmetric carbons at C-2, C-3, C-4 and C-5.

questions.q: The commercial product agar is obtained from
questions.explanation: Agar comes from the red algae Gelidium and Gracilaria.

questions.q: In a lichen, the photosynthetic partner (phycobiont) is
questions.explanation: Lichens are symbiotic associations of algae (phycobiont) that make food and fungi (mycobiont) that absorb water and minerals.

questions.q: The genetic material of tobacco mosaic virus (TMV) is
questions.explanation: TMV is a plant virus with a single-stranded RNA genome.

questions.q: Peat, used as fuel and as packing material for trans-shipment of living material, is obtained from
questions.explanation: Sphagnum, a moss, provides peat and has great water-holding capacity.

questions.q: Pneumatophores, which help in respiration, are found in
questions.explanation: Mangrove plants like Rhizophora have vertically upward aerial roots (pneumatophores) with pores for gaseous exchange.

questions.q: Which of the following is a modified root?
questions.explanation: Carrot is a fusiform modified tap root; potato, ginger and onion are modified stems or underground stem structures.

questions.q: Dumb-bell shaped guard cells are characteristic of the epidermis of
questions.explanation: Guard cells are kidney-shaped in dicots and dumb-bell shaped in grasses.

questions.q: Grass leaves can regrow quickly after being grazed because of
options: the apical meristem at the leaf tip
intercalary meristem at the base of the leaf
questions.explanation: Intercalary meristems at the base of leaves and internodes in grasses allow regeneration after the tips are removed.

questions.q: In the pea flower the stamens are diadelphous (9 + 1). Into how many bundles are the filaments united?
keyPoints: Nine filaments fuse into one bundle
The tenth stamen stays free as the second bundle
questions.explanation: Diadelphous means filaments united in two bundles, 9 + 1 in Fabaceae.

questions.q: The reaction centre chlorophyll a of photosystem II absorbs light best at
questions.explanation: PS II has P680 and PS I has P700.

questions.q: The oxygen released during photosynthesis comes from
questions.explanation: Water is split (photolysis) at photosystem II to release O₂, protons and electrons; this was shown with isotope-labelled oxygen.

questions.q: During light reactions, protons accumulate in the
questions.explanation: Water splitting, plastoquinone proton pumping and NADP reductase cause a build-up of H⁺ in the lumen, whose gradient drives ATP synthase.

questions.q: How many ATP molecules are needed by the Calvin cycle to synthesise one molecule of glucose?
questions.explanation: Per CO₂ the cycle uses 3 ATP and 2 NADPH, so a glucose (6 CO₂) needs 18 ATP and 12 NADPH.

questions.q: In yeast under anaerobic conditions, pyruvic acid is converted to
questions.explanation: Pyruvic acid decarboxylase and alcohol dehydrogenase convert pyruvate to ethanol and CO₂.

questions.q: The hormone that induces stomatal closure under water stress is
questions.explanation: ABA is the stress hormone that causes stomatal closure and promotes seed dormancy.

questions.q: The function of leghaemoglobin in root nodules is to
questions.explanation: Nitrogenase is oxygen-sensitive; the pink leghaemoglobin binds O₂ and maintains anaerobic conditions.

questions.q: Loss of water in liquid form from the tips of leaves through hydathodes at night is called
questions.explanation: Guttation is caused by root pressure when transpiration is low and soil moisture is high.

questions.q: The metal ion acting as a cofactor for the enzyme carboxypeptidase is
questions.explanation: Zinc is the cofactor of the proteolytic enzyme carboxypeptidase.

questions.q: Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a different flower of the same plant is called
questions.explanation: Geitonogamy is genetically similar to autogamy but needs a pollinating agent.

questions.q: At the time of shedding, the pollen grains of most angiosperms are
questions.explanation: In about 60% of angiosperms pollen is shed at the 2-celled stage; the rest at the 3-celled stage.

questions.q: In Mirabilis (or snapdragon), where dominance is incomplete, the phenotypic ratio in the F₂ generation is
questions.explanation: With incomplete dominance the phenotypic ratio equals the genotypic ratio, 1:2:1.

questions.q: ABO blood groups are controlled by three alleles IA, IB and i. How many different genotypes are possible in the human population?
keyPoints: IAIA, IAi, IBIB, IBi, IAIB, ii
questions.explanation: Three alleles taken two at a time give six genotypes (three homozygous and three heterozygous).

questions.q: A carrier woman for colour blindness marries a normal man. The proportion of their sons expected to be colour blind is
questions.explanation: Half of the sons receive the X chromosome carrying the recessive allele from the mother.

questions.q: Okazaki fragments are formed on the
questions.explanation: DNA polymerase works only in the 5′→3′ direction, so the lagging strand is made discontinuously in short Okazaki fragments.

questions.q: For species–area relationships plotted on a log scale, the slope Z of the regression line for smaller areas is typically
questions.explanation: Within similar-sized regions Z lies between 0.1 and 0.2; over very large areas such as whole continents the slope is steeper (0.6 to 1.2).

questions.q: Biomagnification is a particular risk with the pesticide
questions.explanation: DDT is persistent and fat-soluble, so its concentration rises at successive trophic levels, causing eggshell thinning in birds.

questions.topic: Zoology: Animal Diversity and Structural Organisation
questions.q: The collar cells (choanocytes) lining the spongocoel of sponges
options: create the water current and trap food
questions.explanation: Choanocytes beat their flagella to drive water through the canal system and capture food particles.

questions.topic: Zoology: Animal Diversity and Structural Organisation
questions.q: Excretion and osmoregulation in flatworms such as Taenia are carried out by
questions.explanation: Flatworms have flame cells (protonephridia).

questions.topic: Zoology: Animal Diversity and Structural Organisation
questions.q: The rasping, file-like feeding organ found in molluscs is the
questions.explanation: A radula with rows of chitinous teeth occurs in the mouth cavity of most molluscs.

questions.topic: Zoology: Animal Diversity and Structural Organisation
questions.q: Which feature is common to birds and mammals?
questions.explanation: Both groups have a four-chambered heart and are homeothermous; feathers are only in birds and mammary glands only in mammals.

questions.topic: Zoology: Animal Diversity and Structural Organisation
questions.q: Which structure connects a muscle to a bone?
questions.explanation: Tendons are dense regular connective tissue joining muscle to bone; ligaments join bone to bone.

questions.topic: Zoology: Animal Diversity and Structural Organisation
questions.q: In the earthworm, the typhlosole is a fold of the intestinal wall that
options: increases the effective area of absorption
questions.explanation: The median dorsal fold of the intestine, the typhlosole, increases the absorptive surface.

questions.topic: Zoology: Animal Diversity and Structural Organisation
questions.q: How many chambers are present in the heart of a frog?
questions.explanation: Amphibians have a three-chambered heart, so oxygenated and deoxygenated blood mix in the ventricle.

questions.topic: Zoology: Animal Diversity and Structural Organisation
questions.q: A cockroach breathes by a tracheal system opening through how many pairs of spiracles?
questions.explanation: There are ten pairs of spiracles: two thoracic and eight abdominal.

questions.q: The hormone that stimulates the pancreas to release a bicarbonate-rich juice is
questions.explanation: Secretin from the duodenum acts on pancreatic acinar cells to release water and bicarbonate.

questions.q: In blood, most of the carbon dioxide is transported as
questions.explanation: About 70% of CO₂ is carried as bicarbonate, formed with the help of carbonic anhydrase in RBCs.

questions.q: In a normal ECG, the QRS complex represents
questions.explanation: P wave = atrial depolarisation, QRS = ventricular depolarisation (onset of ventricular systole), T wave = ventricular repolarisation.

questions.q: A fall in glomerular blood flow stimulates the release of which substance from the juxtaglomerular cells?
questions.explanation: JG cells release renin, which leads to formation of angiotensin II, raising blood pressure and GFR.

questions.q: Rapid spasms in muscles due to low Ca²⁺ in body fluid is called
questions.explanation: Low calcium increases neuromuscular excitability, causing tetany.

questions.q: The part of the brain containing centres that regulate body temperature, hunger and thirst is the
questions.explanation: The hypothalamus contains neurosecretory cells and centres for temperature regulation, hunger and thirst.

questions.q: Diabetes insipidus results from a deficiency of
questions.explanation: Lack of ADH reduces water reabsorption, leading to excess dilute urine and dehydration.

questions.q: How many bones are present in the skeleton of a normal human adult (as given in NCERT)?
questions.explanation: The adult human skeleton has 206 bones (80 axial and 126 appendicular).

questions.q: Night blindness is caused by deficiency of
questions.explanation: Vitamin A is needed to form rhodopsin in the rods of the retina.

questions.topic: Zoology: Reproduction, Health, Evolution and Biotechnology
questions.q: At birth, the primary oocytes in a human female ovary are
options: arrested at prophase I of meiosis
questions.explanation: Primary oocytes begin meiosis I during foetal life and are arrested at prophase I until puberty.

questions.topic: Zoology: Reproduction, Health, Evolution and Biotechnology
questions.q: Which hormone listed below is produced only by the placenta during pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), hPL and relaxin are produced by the placenta.

questions.topic: Zoology: Reproduction, Health, Evolution and Biotechnology
questions.q: Copper-releasing IUDs like Cu-T prevent pregnancy mainly by
options: suppressing the motility and fertilising capacity of sperm
questions.explanation: Copper ions released by the IUD suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms.

questions.topic: Zoology: Reproduction, Health, Evolution and Biotechnology
questions.q: The gases used in Miller's experiment to simulate the primitive atmosphere were
options: CH₄, NH₃, H₂ and water vapour
questions.explanation: Miller passed electric discharge through CH₄, NH₃, H₂ and water vapour at about 800 °C, forming amino acids.

questions.topic: Zoology: Reproduction, Health, Evolution and Biotechnology
questions.q: The brain capacity of Homo habilis was about
questions.explanation: Homo habilis had a brain capacity of 650–800 cc, Homo erectus about 900 cc and Neanderthals about 1400 cc.

questions.topic: Zoology: Reproduction, Health, Evolution and Biotechnology
questions.q: A single DNA molecule is amplified by PCR with perfect efficiency. How many copies are present after 5 cycles?
questions.explanation: Copies = 2ⁿ, so 2⁵ = 32 after five cycles.

questions.topic: Zoology: Reproduction, Health, Evolution and Biotechnology
questions.q: Bt cotton is resistant to which of the following insect pests?
questions.explanation: Cry genes (such as cryIAc and cryIIAb) of Bacillus thuringiensis make the plant toxic to cotton bollworms.

questions.topic: Zoology: Reproduction, Health, Evolution and Biotechnology
questions.q: The primary lymphoid organs in humans are
questions.explanation: Lymphocytes mature in the bone marrow and thymus; spleen and lymph nodes are secondary lymphoid organs.

questions.topic: Zoology: Reproduction, Health, Evolution and Biotechnology
questions.q: The infective stage of Plasmodium that enters the human body through the bite of a female Anopheles mosquito is the
questions.explanation: Sporozoites in the mosquito's saliva infect liver cells; gametocytes are taken up by the mosquito.
